chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a eunuch who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, then divorced her after consummating the marriage with her. He said: 'She is entitled to the one thousand dirhams that she took from him, and there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: Consummated the marriage (entered into sexual relations)
key_terms.عِدَّةَ: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and waiting period for a eunuch who divorces his wife after consummation?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) ruled that if a eunuch marries a woman, consummates the marriage, and then divorces her, she retains the full dowry (mahr) and is exempt from the waiting period (iddah) typically required for divorce. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction between a eunuch's capacity for marital consummation versus his ability to produce offspring, thereby exempting him from the 'iddah of pregnancy or menstruation. It underscores the principle that the validity of the marital bond and its financial consequences depend on the actualization of conjugal rights rather than mere potential for procreation.
